newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK TROOPS DEPART FOR CHAOTIC ALBANIA.
newsitem.headline: GREEK TROOPS DEPART FOR CHAOTIC ALBANIA.

text.p: About 520 Greek troups participating in the multi-national force to safeguard humanitarian aid in chaotic Albania left on Monday on two tank-landing ships, the defence ministry said.
The Greek navy's Samos and Chios, which are also carrying 92 tanks and armoured vehicles, left the northern Greek port of Salonika in the morning and are expected to reach Albania on Wednesday.
The two Greek ships will arrive either at the Adriatic port of Vlore or Durres, depending on orders from the Italian command, defence ministry sources said.
Greece, concerned with the crisis at its northern border, has already sent 240 soldiers as part of the U.N.-approved Italian-led, eight-nation force of 6,000 soldiers.

The mission of the force, codenamed "Operation Alba" for Italian word for "dawn", is to help distribute much-needed aid to the impoverished Balkan country, which has been racked by violence since an armed uprising erupted following the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes.
Some 300 people have been killed and 700 injured during the weeks of armed anarchy and banditry that have swept Europe's poorest nation.
